item.title: Building k9s for Linode With Bubble Tea
item.description: A lot of my day is spent in k9s, and when I need something from the Linode side of the house (a node that won’t boot, a volume nobody cleaned up, the kubeconfig for a cluster I just made) I’m back in a browser tab or typing linode-cli incantations. I wanted the k9s workflow for the Linode API itself: : to jump to a resource type, / to filter, single-key actions on the selected row, and Enter to go deeper. That turned into linode-tui, a Go TUI built on Bubble Tea, linodego and urfave/cli v3.

item.title: ephemerd: One Daemon, a Fresh Runner Per Job, Every OS
item.description: I have CI that needs Linux amd64, Linux arm64, Windows and macOS, and GitHub-hosted runners for all four get expensive fast, especially the arm64 and Mac minutes. Self-hosted runners fix the bill and create a different problem. A stock actions/runner on a box you own runs whatever the workflow says, keeps whatever the last job left behind, and is one fork PR away from somebody running code on your LAN.

item.title: Stop Ctrl-C-ing Your tail -f | grep
item.description: Here’s a loop I end up in all the time: tail -f app.log, something scrolls by that looks wrong, Ctrl-C, tail -f app.log | grep ERROR, wait for it to happen again, decide I also want to drop the health checks, Ctrl-C, | grep -v healthz, wait again. Every filter tweak throws away the stream and every line that already went past. I got tired of it and wrote tail-gunner, a tail replacement that you can promote into a filtering TUI with one keystroke and drop back out of without the stream ever stopping.
